newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - April 30.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - April 30.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for Reuters by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi Tel:3324842, 3351006, 3761233 Fax:+91-11-3351006 Internet: biznis@giasbm01.vsnl.net.in
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
The Hindustan Times
TAMIL MAANILA CONGRESS DECIDES TO REJOIN GOVERNMENT

Ending 10 days of suspense, the Tamil Maanila Congress (TMC) announced its decision to rejoin the United Front government. Coming as it did on the eve of resumption of the budget session of parliament, TMC chief G.K. Moopanar's announcement brought relief to Prime Minister I.K. Gujral and to the various constituents of the ruling coalition. While P. Chidambaram would be retained as the finance minister to pilot his budget in the crucial session, it was not clear if the other three TMC ministers would be retained.
The Pioneer
MINISTERS JOIN CHORUS FOR LALOO'S OUSTER

Dissidence against Bihar chief minister Laloo Yadav gained momentum even as the Janata Dal legislature party (JDLP) reposed faith in his leadership. At least three senior ministers and 15 legislators came out openly against Yadav while nearly 60 legislators kept away from the JDLP meeting at his residence. The State JD dissidents' described the meeting of the state council, wherein Yadav was authorised to nominate the state party chief and members of the state executive and national council, as unconstitutional.
The Economic Times
LEFT, CONGRESS AGREE TO LET FINANCE BILL SAIL THROUGH

The Left parties and the Congress clarified they would discuss amendments to the Finance Bill but would not obstruct its passage by introducing cut motions. The discussions were likely to take place over the next few days. The Left leaders were satisfied with the prime minister's reassurance that their suggestions would be discussed soon. The Congress party also decided against amendments to the Finance Bill in the shape of cut motions to the demands for grants of various ministries.
CABINET APPROVES BROADCAST BILL

The cabinet cleared the Broadcast Bill and amended the Prasar Bharti Bill. The Broadcast Bill proposes 49 percent foreign equity ventures in broadcasting services, barring terrestrial service. The Bill, as cleared by the cabinet, proposes to grant autonomy to Doordarshan and AIR. It also cleared the decks for the setting up of a broadcast authority to control the media industry. It will also formulate regulations for direct-to home (DTH) services. Another highlight of the bill was the introduction of a licensing system for all private broadcasters.
INDIA URGES WORLD BANK TO DOUBLE LOANS

India urged the World Bank to double its loans from $1 billion a year and also double the International Finance Corporation's programme, now running at $250 million per year. This would be in addition to credit from the International Development Association (IDA) of around $900 million a year. An Indian delegation said the new government would keep economic policies steady and could double its annual World Bank borrowing if the right projects could be found.
Financial Express
MAXTOUCH GETS RESERVE BANK NOD FOR GLOBAL ROAMING SERVICE

The Reserve Bank of India approved the MaxTouch proposal to provide global roaming services, making it the first cellular telephone service operator to get such permission. RBI permission was mandatory for all cellular providers for starting international roaming as the service involved foreign exchange outgo. Hutchison Max, the owner of MaxTouch, was finalising a bilateral agreement with Hutchison Telecom of Hong Kong for such services.
ICICI SETS PRIME LENDING RATES IN 13.5-15 PCT BAND

State owned Industrial Credit and Investment Corporation of India (ICICI) slashed its prime lending rates. It pegged the medium-term lending rate at 13.5 percent with a cap of 17 percent, lower than rates offered by most banks. ICICI also slashed long term prime rates to 15 percent with 18.5 percent at the top end. Both the rates would be effective from May 1.
DEPARTMENT OF TELECOM NOT TO REQUIRE BUDGETARY SUPPORT

The Department of Telecommunications (DoT) would meet its complete requirement of funds in the Ninth Plan period (1997/2002) without any budgetary support. The Communications Ministry, in its plan for telecom services for the Ninth Plan period, estimated the total requirement of funds for DoT at 732.29 billion rupees. For MTNL, the service provider in Delhi and Bombay, DoT would need another 100.21 billion rupees.
EXIM BANK SLASHES EXPORT CREDIT TERM LENDING RATES

The Export Import (Exim) Bank slashed its term loan lending rate to 15 percent from 16.5 and export credit (rupee resources) rate to 14.5 percent. The government also permitted the bank to hold equity investments in joint ventures acquired by Indian companies abroad. It would hold shares of overseas ventures of Indian companies, selling them off later as part of buy back arrangements or through a pull out mechanism arrived at with the company.
Business Standard
INDUSTRY EXPECTS SURGE IN FRESH INVESTMENTS

Corporates reacted cautiously to the cut in prime lending rates by financial institutions and the introduction of a new rate of medium term borrowings at 13.5 per cent by the Industrial Credit and Investment Corporation (ICICI). However, industry associations were more optimistic about the probable impact of the downward trend in interest rates.
RESERVE BANK MAY LIFT CAP ON FINANCIAL INSTITUTION DEPOSITS

The Reserve Bank of India planned to relax the ceiling on deposits raised by financial institutions (FIs). If implemented, the RBI move would permit the FIs easier access to retail investors and lower their cost of resources available for lending. At present, FIs were permitted to raise certificates of deposit, with a tenure of 1-3 years, and fixed deposits with a 3-7 year tenure within prescribed limits, which were last revised in 1992/93.
U.S. INDUSTRY SPLIT OVER STAND ON SPECIAL 301

With the U.S. administration's annual Special 301 exercise, to assess barriers to intellectual property, looming large, two sections of American industry appeared divided on India. The International Intellectual Property Alliance representing the American software, publishing and entertainment industries recommended removing India from the Priority Watchlist. However, the U.S. pharmaceutical industry was lobbying to designate India as a Priority Foreign Country.
FASCEL SIGNS $28 MLN SUPPLIER'S CREDIT DEAL

Fascel, the Gujarat cellular telephone service licensee, signed a $28 million supplier's credit deal with Finnish Export Credit (FEC). The first of its kind in the Indian cellular industry, the credit agreement would fund a GSM cellular equipment purchase from Nokia. FEC would extend 85 percent of the loan while the remaining 15 percent would be raised from commercial banks.
The Observer
FOREIGN INVESTMENT VIA MAURITIUS UNDER PROBE

The government was probing foreign investments coming into India through Mauritius. In the past few months, the government was constantly alerted by international agencies of illegal funds entering the country through Mauritius. These funds, which were coming mainly through portfolio investments, were learnt to be drug money. Both the finance and the industry ministries were separately looking into Mauritian investments in India.
